This is also the better shape: `INSERT OR IGNORE` silently skips an existing row, so `plan='pro'` would never repair a row created without it, and the process would look successful while not being one. Documented with the reasoning in-file.

nodes.label: Read-only intent proved behaviourally by SQLite refusing writes with SQLITE_READONLY
nodes.norm_label: read-only intent proved behaviourally by sqlite refusing writes with sqlite_readonly
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-10-02 - t2-readonly-db-layer [ses_f05f6e5b1ffe7Yovj79hzd2lpE].md:L2670] Not by inspecting a flag. After `openReadonly`, real `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `CREATE TABLE`, and `PRAGMA user_version = 99` are each refused by **SQLite itself** with `err.code === 'SQLITE_READONLY'`, including inside an explicit `BEGIN`/`ROLLBACK` transaction. Post-failure assertions confirm nothing half-applied. `openReadonly` on a missing path throws `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` and leaves no file on disk.
